Offline, two other hypotheses I tested and rejected before choosing this one: (a) the prior is wrong because the generator draws gate structures, not tables. On the 30 determined triples from b0-b2 traces (deduced from answers in the .md files, not from gold), the parent's uniform-over-(split, table) prior has the best log-likelihood (-216.6), vs -223.8 for structure counts with multinomial split weights and -244.8 for a random-process prior. (b) the query count tail is myopic greedy. A 2-step lookahead ranking was slightly worse in simulation (mean 11.44 vs 11.08 queries, max 17 vs 16 over 300 runs).

risks: The outcome is already saturated (parent 10/10). This change removes wasted model calls but cannot raise the final-table rate on this batch, and does not lower queries (12.2 vs 12.1, within noise).

With ready-made tags in the list, the model copies the first one more often (85% vs 66%). Its choice is still its own and the harness still accepts any informative query, but its free reasoning now has even less effect on which query is sent.

Every turn prompt changed, so all replies are fresh samples at temperature 0.7, not cache replays. One run of 122 replies supports the effect, but rare format slips, such as echoing the whole list (the first tag would then be taken), have not been seen yet and are not specifically handled.

The parent's misleading docstring hid that a misread rule space would give a confidently wrong table, with no check of implied rows. That is still true. The space matches the system-prompt rules exactly, so it is not expected to matter.
